overview: A ten-pitch trad line linking cracks and corners with a few face moves protected by bolts. Pitch grades run 5.10a, 5.8, 5.10a (5.9 if the corner is taken instead), 5.9+, 5.10a, 5.11b, 5.10b, 5.10a, and finally the 5.12a exit corner past bolts. The Angishore Finish, an option from pitch 7, follows the corner above (5.9+) and ends at a belay on the left that is exposed, then 4th class for 200'. The standard last pitch covers 200' of 4th and easy 5th class. Every belay except the first is believed to have 2 bolts. If rappelling, make the last rap to the traverse ledge from the Screech topout anchors.
A scrambly four-pitch outing along the canyon side with two short overhang moves and a buttress finish.

A 12-pitch line on the South Face of Charlotte Dome, starting at the right side of a small bowl; ratings are approximate. Pitches 2 and 3 (5.9, protection thin or poor) trend right and up, past a bolt, with some lichen. Pitch 5 climbs an easy dihedral, then a groove with sparse protection, at 5.10a. Pitch 8 (5.8, runout) has few placements and long stretches of friction with no pro. The upper pitches ease to 5.5, then third class along the ridge to the summit. Descent: do not drop off early; first traverse far to the north, with exposure for about 500 feet.

A 200 ft sky route that can only be reached by rappel. Step off the hanging belay onto leaning, overhanging offset stacks on red Camalots, rest, then kick out to a steeper angle and finish by campusing leftward and mantling at the anchor. Compared with Six Star Crack, it is harder, steeper and a bit shorter. Two 10 ft blank sections make ground-up free climbing practically impossible; the author does not want a bolt ladder. Remove fixed lines promptly after use.
